correctness.rationale: The genuine Laplace transform of the radius-t Fourier integral is 8s²/Π(s²+4π²k_j²); inversion at t=1 gives coefficient 4/3 at origin, 2/(π²a²) on a nonzero axis, −1/(4π²a²) at (a,a,a), 1/[π²(b²−a²)] at (a,a,b), all remaining frequencies zero. Counting reflection-plane integer triples yields 24N²+2N+1 (including N=0). Nonzero coefficients are degree −2 homogeneous along integer frequency rays, so periodized integer m dilates satisfy P_m=4(m³−m)/3+mP_1 by Fourier uniqueness; an independent octant/complementary-ratio count in the package gives the same identity. Three mutually adjacent lattice centers cannot be within strict l1 radius one; pairwise adjacent-center overlap volume equals 1/6, giving E[P1]=4/3 and E[binom(P1,2)]=1/2 and probabilities (1/6,1/3,1/2). Independent direct enumeration for generic rational shifts through radius five matched the identity; it is not the proof for all m.
